subject: POC Plan: Acme Corp — Redwood integration, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Jane Smith <jane.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC Plan: Acme Corp — Redwood integration, success criteria & next steps

Hi John / Jane —

Great to meet with you earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we can lock the POC scope and timelines.

Recap (from today’s call):
- Objective: Validate Redwood for in-product summarization and search relevance on Acme’s customer support corpus.
- Primary success criteria:
  - Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-turn summarization (seq len ~512)
  - Throughput: sustain 20 qps for batch evaluation during peak window
  - Quality: > 85% relevance on your internal rubric (we’ll align on a 20-item prompt set)
  - Stability: no more than 1% error rate over a 24-hour run
- Evaluation plan: run a 2-week trial against a representative dataset, measure metrics above and gather human evals on 200 samples.
- Key owners:
  - Acme: John (product) + Jane (platform/infra)
  - Redwood: Marissa (engagement lead) + Dev (integration/SE) + Rishi (commercial lead)

Integration checklist (initial):
- SDK: use Redwood Node/Python SDK for session management and streaming. We’ll provide the SDK package and quickstart example.
- API routes: text generation (/v1/generate), chat (/v1/chat), embeddings (/v1/embeddings). We recommend using chat for conversational summarization with tool-calling disabled initially.
- Streaming: enable token streaming for UI responsiveness — SDK has a streaming client example (attached).
- Tool calling: postpone for initial run; if you want structured extraction we can enable function call schemas in week 2.

Attachments: acme-poc-plan-v1.pdf (POC plan), redwood-sdk-integration-guide.zip (examples + streaming client).

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): confirm success criteria + sign MPO/POC MSA and scope
- Week 1: provide SDK + sample code; Acme devs run integration smoke test
- Week 2-3: run evaluation jobs and collect metrics + human evals
- Week 4: review results, recommend rollout path / production topology

Next steps (please reply with):
1) Confirm the success criteria above or suggest edits by EOD Friday (5/21).
2) Share a sample of the dataset access method (S3 link / temporary export) and ideal 20-item prompt set.
3) Confirm who on your team will run the smoke test and available times for a 30-min integration walkthrough next week.

I’ll schedule the walkthrough once we hear back and will share the HubSpot/Metrics board link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: POC Plan: Acme Corp — Redwood integration, success criteria & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick confirmations and questions from our side: 

Confirmations:
- We’re aligned on the primary success criteria (latency/throughput/quality/stability).
- We can commit to running the 2-week trial once integration is complete.

Questions / clarifications:
1) For latency numbers: is the 95th <350ms measured from our client to Redwood (including network) or just Redwood processing time? We need to understand the SLO boundary.
2) SDK: we primarily use Python. Will the SDK include the streaming client and an example with async io?
3) Data access: we can share a temporary S3 bucket with a subset (~5k records) by COB Monday. Any format constraints?

Partial answers:
- We’ll have Emily (platform) run the smoke test; I’ll confirm calendar availability tomorrow.

Thanks — John
John Doe

john.doe@acme.com

Subject: Re: POC Plan: Acme Corp — Redwood integration, success criteria & next steps

Hi John — thanks, great questions. Answers below and next actions.

1) Latency SLO boundary: the 95th <350ms is Redwood processing time (server-side). We typically add a ~50-100ms network budget depending on region; we’ll capture end-to-end numbers during the smoke test. If you need client-to-client SLOs we can create an E2E measurement in week 1.

2) SDK: yes — Python SDK includes async streaming examples. The attached redwood-sdk-integration-guide.zip contains:
- async_streaming_example.py (Python asyncio example)
- node_streaming_example.js
- instructions.md (how to run locally)

3) Data format: S3 CSV/JSONL with one record per line is ideal. Please include an id, text, and metadata fields. We’ll provide a small ingestion script if needed.

Proposed owners & timeline (updated):
- Marissa (Redwood): engagement lead — scheduling, results review
- Dev (Redwood): SE — integration support, smoke test troubleshooting
- Rishi (Redwood): commercial — contract/POC terms
- John (Acme): product lead — success criteria signoff
- Jane / Emily (Acme): platform — provide S3 + run smoke tests

Kickoff slots (30 min integration walkthrough):
- Tue 5/19 11:00-11:30 PT
- Wed 5/20 10:00-10:30 PT
- Thu 5/21 14:00-14:30 PT

Next steps:
- John/Jane: share S3 link + sample prompt set (by COB Mon 5/18) — we can start staging data.
- Dev: will run an initial connectivity test once keys are shared.
- Marissa: will upload the POC board in HubSpot and share the Drive folder (links below).

Links: HubSpot — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/ACME-POC-128
Drive — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/driveid-acme-poc

If one of the kickoff slots works, please reply with the preferred time and we’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Marissa
